posts.title: Why Your Website Budget Is Probably Wrong (And How to Get It Right)
posts.excerpt: Most Saudi businesses either massively overpay or get cheap sites that don't work. Here's how to budget smartly — real numbers, real scenarios, no fluff.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
Last month, a clinic in Riyadh told us they'd been quoted 45,000 SAR for a 5-page website. A week later, a restaurant owner in Jeddah asked if 500 SAR was enough for a "simple site." Both budgets are wrong — and both business owners are losing money because of it.

The clinic would overpay by 40,000 SAR for a site that wouldn't generate a single extra patient. The restaurant would get a site that loads slowly, ranks nowhere on Google, and needs rebuilding within 6 months. The real problem isn't how much you spend — it's that nobody tells you what to spend on and what to skip.

We've built over 40 websites for Saudi businesses in the past year. We've seen every budget mistake, every hidden cost, every regret. This guide walks you through exactly how to build a website budget that makes sense for your specific business — whether you're a clinic in Riyadh, a restaurant in Jeddah, or a furniture store in Dammam.

The Two Budget Traps Every Saudi Business Falls Into

Trap #1: The Overpayer — Spending 30,000+ SAR on What Should Cost 3,000

Some agencies in Riyadh charge 30,000-50,000 SAR for what is essentially a 5-page corporate website with a basic contact form. The pitch sounds impressive: "custom design from scratch," "bespoke functionality," "enterprise architecture." But when you peel back the layers, you're paying for a slow, over-engineered site that took 4 months to build and delivers the same results as a well-built 5,000 SAR site.

Why does this happen? Many agencies charge based on what they think you'll pay, not what the work actually costs. They add "strategy fees," "project management fees," "QA fees" — line items that inflate the bill without improving your outcome. A 5-page corporate website does not need 4 months and 5 people to build.

Real example: A logistics company in Dammam came to us after paying 38,000 SAR to a premium agency. Their site had 17 plugins, an elaborate animation framework using Three.js, and a loading time of 9 seconds. Their bounce rate was 83% — meaning 83 out of every 100 visitors left before the page finished loading. We rebuilt it for 3,500 SAR: 5 pages, clean HTML, optimized images, proper caching, and only the essential functionality. Loading time dropped to 1.2 seconds. Bounce rate dropped to 41%. Their phone started ringing within a week. The previous site was "premium" in name only — it actually hurt their business.

Trap #2: The Bargain Hunter — Paying 500-1,000 SAR for a Site That Never Works

Sites on freelancer platforms for 500-1,000 SAR are tempting, especially when you're starting out. But here's what you're actually getting: a pre-made template with your logo slapped on, no SEO setup whatsoever, generic stock photos that other 500 sites also use, no mobile optimization testing, hosting on a cheap shared server that loads at 8+ seconds, and zero support when something inevitably breaks.

Why do people choose this? Because the upfront cost is low and the promises are high. The freelancer shows you beautiful portfolio examples (which they didn't actually build), promises delivery in 3 days, and disappears after payment. Six months later, you discover your site has been hacked, your hosting was never properly secured, and you're ranking on page 12 of Google. The cheap site ends up costing more than doing it right.

Real example: A restaurant in Jeddah paid 800 SAR for a "complete website." The freelancer used a free WordPress theme, installed it on budget shared hosting (the kind that hosts 200 sites on one server), and disappeared. Six months later, the site was hacked through an outdated plugin, loading in 14 seconds (Google's Core Web Vitals gave it an F rating), and ranking nowhere. The restaurant spent 2,500 SAR to clean up the malware, migrate to proper hosting, and rebuild with SEO — three times the original cost.

How to Budget Smartly: The Real Breakdown We Use with Clients

After 40+ projects across Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Khobar, Mecca, and Medina, here are the real numbers. These aren't estimates — they're what we and other reputable Saudi agencies actually charge.

Simple Corporate Site (3-5 pages): 1,000 — 2,000 SAR

For a corporate website — homepage, about, services, contact — 1,000-1,500 SAR if you have your content and logo ready. Add 500 SAR for professional Arabic content writing, which we strongly recommend. Writing your own content might save money upfront, but it almost always results in weaker copy that doesn't convert.

What's included at this price: responsive design that works on all devices, basic SEO (meta tags, sitemap, robots.txt), free SSL certificate, contact form with spam protection, WhatsApp click-to-chat integration, hosting setup, and one round of revisions. Build time: 5-7 business days.

Smart money move: Instead of spending 5,000 SAR extra on a "premium design," invest 1,000 SAR in local SEO — Google Business Profile optimization, local keyword targeting, and citation building. A simple site on page 1 of Google outperforms a beautiful site on page 5 literally 100% of the time. We've seen a dental clinic in Al-Olaya, Riyadh get more WhatsApp inquiries from a clean 4-page site with proper local SEO than their previous elaborate 20-page site that cost 5x more.

WordPress Site (5-15 pages): 1,500 — 3,000 SAR

A WordPress site with a custom-designed theme runs 1,500-2,500 SAR depending on complexity. We use Elementor Pro for clients who want to edit content themselves — it's the most user-friendly option for Arabic content editing, with full RTL support out of the box.

The hidden cost no agency mentions until after you sign: WordPress requires ongoing maintenance. Budget 200-400 SAR/month for managed WordPress hosting (not the cheap shared kind), SSL certificate renewal, plugin and theme updates (typically 10-20 updates per month), security monitoring, weekly backups, and performance optimization. A neglected WordPress site gets hacked within 6-12 months on average. We include 3 months of free maintenance with every build so you can experience the value before committing to a monthly plan.

When WordPress makes sense: You need a blog that Google actually indexes (WordPress's blog architecture is still the best for SEO), you want full control over your content, you need integrations with CRMs or email marketing tools, or you plan to scale your site significantly over time.

Online Store: 2,000 — 5,000 SAR

E-commerce pricing varies the most because the platform choice dramatically affects both setup cost and ongoing expenses. Here's our real data from 20+ stores built on all three platforms:

  • Salla stores: 1,500-3,000 SAR setup. Arabic-first interface means faster configuration. Native Mada, STC Pay, and Apple Pay integration without third-party apps. Monthly subscription: 99 SAR. Zero transaction fees on Mada. Best for local-focused Saudi businesses.
  • Shopify stores: 2,500-4,000 SAR setup. Superior design customization through Liquid templates. Better blogging platform. But needs paid apps for Saudi payment gateways (typically 20-50 SAR/month extra). Monthly subscription: $29-79/month (109-300 SAR) + 2.9% + 2.40 SAR per transaction. Best for brands targeting international markets or needing custom design.
  • Custom e-commerce: 5,000-15,000 SAR. Only justified for businesses with unique needs like multi-vendor marketplaces, subscription models, B2B wholesale portals, or complex inventory across multiple warehouses.

The Hidden Costs Nobody Warns You About (Year One)

Every first-time client is surprised by these. Let's put everything on the table:

  • Hosting: 200-400 SAR/month for a plan that won't crash during your first ad campaign. The 20 SAR/month specials host 100+ sites per server — your site will be slow and vulnerable.
  • SSL certificate: Free with proper hosting (Let's Encrypt). If an agency charges you extra for SSL, that's a red flag.
  • Professional email: Google Workspace at 20 SAR/user/month. An info@yourcompany.com address is non-negotiable for looking legitimate to Saudi customers.
  • Arabic content writing: 500-1,500 SAR depending on page count. AI-generated Arabic text is obvious to native speakers and damages trust. Professional Arabic copy is an investment, not an expense.
  • SEO setup + 3 months: 4,000-8,000 SAR. A website without SEO is like a shop in the desert with no road signs. You can build the most beautiful shop in the world — if nobody can find it, it's worthless.
  • Monthly maintenance: 200-500 SAR. Software updates, security patches, performance checks, content updates. Think of this as insurance — it prevents the much larger cost of recovering from a hack or a crashed site.

Where to Save vs. Where to Invest

After 40+ projects, here's our definitive list:

Save your money on:

  • Custom illustrations and complex animations (visitors come for information, not entertainment)
  • Premium stock photo subscriptions (Unsplash and Pexels have high-quality free options)
  • Multi-language support from day one (add Arabic first, expand when you have traffic in other markets)
  • Expensive page builders with features you'll never use
  • "Strategy fees" and "brand discovery workshops" for a simple corporate site

Invest in:

  • Professional Arabic content writing (your words represent your business to every visitor)
  • SEO setup + the first 3 months of optimization (this is what makes your site findable)
  • Quality hosting with Saudi or GCC servers (local hosting = faster loading for Saudi users)
  • Thorough mobile testing across real devices (most Saudi users browse on mobile)
  • WhatsApp Business API integration (Saudi customers prefer WhatsApp over email and contact forms)

Sample Year-One Budgets for Different Scenarios

Scenario A: Small business in Riyadh — corporate site

  • Website build: 1,500 SAR
  • Arabic content writing: 1,000 SAR
  • Hosting + maintenance (12 months): 3,600 SAR
  • Local SEO setup + 3 months: 4,000 SAR
  • Google Workspace (1 user, 12 months): 240 SAR
  • Total: 10,340 SAR

Scenario B: E-commerce brand in Jeddah — Salla store

  • Salla store setup: 2,500 SAR
  • Product content writing (50 products): 2,500 SAR
  • Salla subscription (12 months): 1,188 SAR
  • Product photography: 2,000 SAR
  • SEO setup + 3 months: 6,000 SAR
  • Snapchat/TikTok ad setup: 1,500 SAR
  • Total: 15,688 SAR

Scenario C: Professional service in Dammam — WordPress site

  • WordPress build with blog: 2,500 SAR
  • Arabic content + 4 blog posts: 2,000 SAR
  • Hosting + maintenance (12 months): 4,800 SAR
  • SEO content strategy + 3 months: 6,000 SAR
  • Total: 15,300 SAR

Compare any of these to the 45,000 SAR the clinic was quoted — or the 800 SAR the restaurant wasted. The middle path isn't just more affordable; it's what actually works.

Final Word: Budget Right, Build Once

The businesses that succeed online in Saudi Arabia aren't the ones that spend the most. They're the ones that spend smart — investing in what drives real results (SEO, content quality, site speed, mobile experience) and skipping what doesn't (fancy animations, over-engineering, unnecessary features). A well-budgeted website built once with the right priorities will outperform a poorly-budgeted site rebuilt twice.

If you're planning a website or online store and want honest guidance on what to spend, we offer a free 15-minute consultation. We'll look at your business, your goals, and your budget — and give you a straight answer about what you actually need. No pressure, no upsell. Just real advice from people who've done this 40+ times across Saudi Arabia.

posts.title: Still Choosing Between Shopify and Salla? Here's What Actually Matters for Your Saudi Business
posts.excerpt: We've built 20+ stores on both platforms. Instead of listing features, we'll tell you which one made more money for each type of business — and why.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
You've read the comparison articles. You've watched the YouTube videos comparing dashboard screenshots. You've asked your friends who run online stores. And somehow, you're still confused about whether to choose Shopify or Salla for your Saudi e-commerce business.

That confusion isn't your fault. Almost every comparison you'll find lists features side by side — Salla has X, Shopify has Y — without answering the only question that matters: which platform will make your specific business more money?

We've built over 20 e-commerce stores on both platforms in the past year. We've seen which ones succeed, which ones struggle, and exactly why. Instead of another feature table that leaves you more confused, here are three real stories of Saudi businesses — and which platform was right for each.

The Three Scenarios: Real Businesses, Real Decisions

Scenario #1: Ahmed's Perfume Store in Riyadh

Ahmed sells luxury Arabian perfumes — oud, musk, and traditional blends. His customers are primarily in Riyadh and Jeddah, mostly Saudi nationals and GCC residents. He needed a clean store with professional product photos, detailed descriptions in Arabic and English, and most importantly — seamless checkout with Mada, STC Pay, and Apple Pay. Ahmed is not tech-savvy; he needed something he could manage himself.

We recommended Salla. Here's why:

Ahmed's customers are 100% local. They pay with Mada (over 70% of Saudi online transactions use Mada). They expect checkout in 30 seconds, not 2 minutes with redirects. Salla's native integration with Saudi payment gateways meant customers completed checkout on the store itself — no redirecting to a third-party payment page that looks unfamiliar and causes abandonment.

The numbers from Ahmed's first quarter: store built and live in 5 days. Setup cost: 2,500 SAR. Monthly subscription: 99 SAR. In the first month, 187 orders processed with a 3.4% checkout completion rate. Across 12 similar stores we track, the average Shopify checkout completion for Saudi stores is 2.7%. That 0.7% difference translates to roughly 4-5 extra orders per 1,000 visitors. For a store doing 50,000 SAR/month in traffic value, that's an estimated 2,100 SAR/month in additional revenue — far more than Salla's subscription cost.

Ahmed also benefited from Salla's Arabic-first admin panel. He manages his store entirely in Arabic, without needing English or technical support. When he had a question at 11 PM during Ramadan sales, Salla's Arabic WhatsApp support responded in 15 minutes. That level of support simply doesn't exist on Shopify.

Why Salla won here: Native payment gateways, Arabic-first experience, local support, lower cost, and faster setup. Ahmed needed Saudi features, not international features.

Scenario #2: Noura's Fashion Brand (Saudi Arabia + UAE)

Noura designs contemporary abayas — modern cuts, premium fabrics, limited collections. She ships to both Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Her customers expect a premium brand experience: editorial-quality product pages, a distinctive visual identity, a blog that tells her brand story, and seamless multi-currency shopping.

We recommended Shopify. Here's why:

Shopify's theme customization is significantly more powerful than Salla's. Noura needed custom typography that matched her brand, unique product page layouts with lookbook-style galleries, a video background on her homepage, and a blog that could rank on Google for e-commerce SEO keywords. Shopify's Liquid template engine and the vast ecosystem of premium themes made this possible without needing custom development from scratch.

For multi-currency, Shopify Markets handled SAR and AED pricing automatically based on the customer's location — Noura didn't need to manage two separate stores. For shipping, Shopify's integration with ShipStation and local carriers made UAE delivery seamless with tracking updates in both Arabic and English.

The cost trade-off was significant. Shopify setup: 3,500 SAR. Monthly subscription at the Basic plan: approximately 109 SAR/month (converted from $29) plus 2.9% + 2.40 SAR per transaction. Over 12 months with 200,000 SAR in sales, Noura paid roughly 7,000 SAR in Shopify fees compared to 1,188 SAR on Salla. But her average order value was 320 SAR — significantly above the Saudi Shopify average of 210 SAR. The premium brand experience that Shopify enabled justified the higher prices.

Why Shopify won here: Brand differentiation was critical, international customers mattered, the blog platform drove organic traffic, and higher order values offset the higher platform costs.

Scenario #3: Fahad's Electronics Store in Dammam

Fahad sells phone accessories, chargers, headphones, and cables. His margins are razor-thin — typically 15-20%. His customers are price-sensitive; they compare prices across multiple stores before buying. He also wanted to run Snapchat and TikTok ads to drive traffic, which means unpredictable traffic spikes.

This is the hardest scenario for any online store. Thin margins make every riyal of platform fees painful. Price-sensitive customers mean every conversion point in the checkout flow matters. And ad-driven traffic spikes mean the store infrastructure must handle sudden load without crashing.

We recommended Salla. Here's the math that sealed the decision:

Fahad's projected first-year sales: 180,000 SAR.

  • Salla cost: 99 SAR/month × 12 = 1,188 SAR/year. Zero transaction fees on Mada. Total platform cost: 1,188 SAR.
  • Shopify Basic cost: 109 SAR/month × 12 = 1,308 SAR. Plus 2.9% transaction fees on 180,000 SAR = 5,220 SAR. Total platform cost: 6,528 SAR.

That's a difference of 5,340 SAR per year — more than four times Salla's annual subscription. For a business with 15% margins on 180,000 SAR in sales (gross profit of 27,000 SAR), platform fees alone represent 24% of gross profit on Shopify versus 4% on Salla. That's the difference between healthy profitability and scraping by.

Beyond cost, Salla handled Fahad's traffic spikes better. During an aggressive 3-day Snapchat ad campaign, Fahad's store received 12,000 visitors in a single day. Salla's cloud infrastructure absorbed it without any slowdown. We've seen Shopify stores on lower-tier plans crash or slow to a crawl under similar ad-driven loads — costing thousands in lost sales during peak traffic.

Third, Salla's Saudi-specific shipping integrations gave Fahad a competitive advantage. He connected directly with SMSA and Aramex through Salla's API, set up automated shipping label generation, and offered same-day delivery in Dammam — a promise that increased his checkout conversion by 18% compared to stores with standard 2-3 day delivery.

Why Salla won here: Lower platform fees preserved thin margins, infrastructure handled ad traffic spikes reliably, and local shipping integrations created a competitive advantage that directly increased sales.

Beyond the Stories: A Honest Look at the Feature Gap

Let's address what Shopify advocates will tell you. Yes, Shopify's app ecosystem is larger — over 8,000 apps compared to Salla's 200+. Yes, Shopify's blog platform is better for SEO. Yes, Shopify's theme marketplace offers more design variety.

But here's what we've learned from 20+ stores: most Saudi e-commerce businesses use less than 20% of Shopify's features. The other 80% is complexity and cost they never needed. They pay for an enterprise suite when they need a focused e-commerce tool.

Meanwhile, Salla has been closing the gap aggressively. In the last 18 months alone, Salla added:

  • Custom meta titles, descriptions, and URL slugs for SEO
  • A native loyalty and rewards program
  • Advanced discount rules, BOGO offers, and flash sale scheduling
  • Multi-branch inventory management (critical for businesses with physical locations)
  • Enhanced analytics with customer lifetime value tracking
  • Integration with Saudi-specific logistics providers (SMSA, Aramex, Saudi Post, Fetchr)
  • Improved checkout flow with one-click purchase options

Are there still gaps? Absolutely. If you need a subscription-based store (recurring billing), a multi-vendor marketplace, deep CRM or ERP integration, or advanced multi-language for 5+ languages, Shopify (or custom development) is likely the better choice. But for 80% of Saudi SMEs — especially those just starting e-commerce — Salla is the smarter financial decision.

The Decision Framework We Use with Every Client

Here's how we make the call in under 30 minutes with complete confidence:

  • Choose Salla if: Your customers are primarily in Saudi Arabia or the GCC, you accept Mada as a primary payment method, you want to be live in under 2 weeks, cost predictability matters to your business model, and you prefer managing your store in Arabic. Most Saudi e-commerce businesses — probably 80% — fall squarely in this category.
  • Choose Shopify if: You're selling internationally (multiple currencies, multiple countries), you need a highly customized brand experience with unique design, content marketing and blogging are central to your customer acquisition strategy, or you need specific third-party apps for your niche that Salla doesn't offer.
  • Choose custom development if: You have genuinely unique business model requirements — marketplace, subscription, B2B wholesale portal with tiered pricing, or integrations with legacy ERP systems. This typically starts at 15,000 SAR and only makes sense if your revenue justifies it.

Our honest advice: If you're unsure, start with Salla. You can always migrate to Shopify later if you outgrow the platform — we've done migrations in both directions. The cost of starting on Shopify when Salla would have worked (thousands in unnecessary fees) is significantly higher than starting on Salla and upgrading to Shopify when your business actually needs it.

The Real Cost of Indecision

The worst choice isn't choosing the wrong platform — it's spending three months comparing platforms, watching review videos, and reading forums while your competitors are already selling. Every month you wait is a month of revenue you're not earning, customer data you're not collecting, and market position you're not building.

We've helped over 20 Saudi businesses make this decision and launch their stores. If you want our honest, no-obligation recommendation for your specific business — tell us what you sell, who you sell to, and where you're based — we'll give you a clear answer in a 15-minute call. No charge, no commitment, just the clarity you need to move forward.

posts.title: Why Your Salla Store Isn't Ranking on Google (And Exactly How to Fix It)
posts.excerpt: You built a beautiful Salla store, invested in products and photos — but nobody can find you on Google. Here are the specific fixes that work for Saudi Salla stores.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
You did everything right. You picked great products, took professional photos with proper lighting, set up your Salla store with a clean theme, wrote product descriptions, and launched with excitement. Then weeks passed. Then months. And the only traffic you're getting is when you personally share the link on WhatsApp or Instagram.

This is the most common frustration we hear from Salla store owners across Saudi Arabia. The platform makes it incredibly easy to build a beautiful store — but it doesn't make it easy to get found on Google. Salla's default SEO setup is minimal by design, and most store owners either don't know what needs fixing or assume Google will figure it out. Google won't.

We've optimized over 15 Salla stores for Google in the past year. Some went from page 5 to page 1 for their target keywords. Others barely moved. The difference wasn't the SEO strategy — it was knowing exactly which Salla-specific levers to pull and in what order.

This guide covers every fix we've tested, every mistake we've seen, and the exact sequence we follow to get Salla stores ranking on Google.

The #1 Problem: Salla's Default Product Titles Are Ranking Killers

Here's what Salla does by default when you add a product: it takes the product name you entered and uses it as the HTML page title exactly as-is. If you named your product "ساعة يدوية" (wristwatch), your page title in Google's index is literally "ساعة يدوية." That single generic phrase is competing against millions of other pages — including Amazon, Noon, and every other e-commerce site selling watches.

This is the single biggest SEO mistake we see on Salla stores. And the good news: it's the easiest and fastest fix, with the highest return on time invested.

The fix: Salla allows you to set a custom SEO title for each product and category page. Go to Products → select a product → SEO settings → override the auto-generated title. Instead of "ساعة يدوية," use something like this:

  • ❌ "ساعة يدوية" — too generic, competing with millions
  • ✅ "ساعة يدوية رجالية مقاومة للماء — توصيل مجاني في الرياض" — specific product type, benefit, location, and buying incentive all in one title

Real result: We changed product titles for a small accessories shop in Riyadh. Same products, same prices, same images — we only changed the SEO titles to include product attributes, benefits, and location mentions. Their organic traffic increased 340% in 6 weeks. The cost: about 3 hours of work. The return: thousands of additional monthly visitors. Google needs context to rank pages, and Salla's default setup provides almost none.

What Salla Handles Well (Don't Waste Time and Budget Here)

Before detailing the fixes, let's be fair about what Salla handles automatically so you can focus your energy where it matters:

  • SSL certificate: Automatic with Let's Encrypt, free, and always updated. No action needed from you.
  • Mobile responsiveness: All Salla official themes are mobile-optimized. Google's Mobile-Friendly Test consistently passes for Salla stores using official themes.
  • XML sitemap generation: Salla generates a basic sitemap automatically and updates it when you add products. However, it may not include blog pages if you're using Salla's built-in blog feature.
  • CDN and hosting infrastructure: Salla's cloud is robust. Page speed Core Web Vitals scores are generally good without optimization — a significant advantage over self-hosted solutions.
  • Canonical tags: Salla handles canonical URLs for product and category pages correctly, preventing duplicate content issues.

What Salla does NOT handle and you must fix manually: Meta descriptions (auto-generated and often poor), category descriptions (default: blank — a massive missed opportunity), product schema (not added automatically), URL slug optimization (limited but improvable), image alt text (not auto-generated), breadcrumb schema (not added), blog post SEO, and Open Graph tags for social sharing.

The Exact Fixes That Move Rankings

These are ordered by impact, from highest to lowest. Start with #1 and work your way down.

Fix #1: Custom Meta Descriptions (20-30% CTR Improvement)

Salla auto-generates meta descriptions by taking the first 155 characters of your product description. In Arabic, this is particularly problematic — Arabic text often has shorter sentences and more repetition, meaning the auto-generated description frequently cuts off mid-sentence or, worse, pulls in English placeholder text if your product description starts with English measurements or brand names.

When Google sees a truncated or nonsensical meta description, it ignores it and pulls a random sentence from your page instead. That random sentence is almost never optimized to make someone click.

Action: Write a custom Arabic meta description (150-160 characters) for every product, starting with the highest-traffic products. Formula: primary keyword + key benefit + location mention + call-to-action. Example: "اشتري ساعة يدوية رجالية مقاومة للماء بأفضل سعر في السعودية. توصيل مجاني للرياض وجدة. ضمان سنتان. اطلب الآن."

Real result: For a Salla store selling skincare products in Jeddah, we wrote custom meta descriptions for their top 30 products. Their organic click-through rate (CTR) from Google search results jumped from 1.8% to 3.2% — nearly double. That single fix drove more traffic than any other effort we made. E-commerce SEO is often won or lost at the meta description level because it directly affects how many searchers choose your result over competitors.

Fix #2: Category Descriptions (Fastest Wins)

Salla allows you to add a description to each category page. Over 90% of Salla stores leave this field completely blank. This is one of the most painfully obvious missed opportunities in Saudi e-commerce SEO.

Category pages are often the most visited pages on an e-commerce site after the homepage. They have high authority in Google's eyes because they link to multiple products. But with no description, Google has very little context about what the category is about beyond the product titles within it.

Action: Write 200-300 word Arabic descriptions for every category page. Use the primary keyword 3-4 times naturally (not stuffed — in natural Arabic sentences that a human would actually write). Mention related sub-categories, key brands or product types, and include 2-3 internal links to specific products or sub-categories. End with a sentence that encourages browsing or purchasing.

Real result: For a Salla beauty store, we added a 250-word description to their "مرطب للوجه" (face moisturizer) category page. That single page went from position 34 to position 8 in Google in 2 months. It now brings in approximately 1,200 organic visitors per month — all from a 30-minute content investment that cost nothing but time. Content SEO on category pages is the fastest win for any Salla store, bar none.

Fix #3: URL Optimization (Work Around Salla's Limitations)

This is the one area where Salla genuinely frustrates us as SEO specialists. Salla's URL structure is more rigid than Shopify's or custom platforms. You may end up with URLs like salla.sa/store-name/products/23748 instead of salla.sa/store/ساعة-يدوية-رجالية.

While you cannot change the entire URL structure, Salla does allow you to customize the URL slug in the SEO settings for each product. This is a setting many store owners miss entirely, leaving the default numeric or transliterated slug.

Action: In each product's SEO settings, set a clean Arabic or English URL slug that includes the primary keyword. Short, descriptive slugs help Google understand the page topic and look more professional in search results. Also, ensure your store uses a custom domain (not the default salla.sa subdomain). A custom domain signals to Google that you're a legitimate independent business, not a template store. This alone can improve rankings by a measurable margin.

Fix #4: Structured Data (Product Schema)

Salla does not automatically add Product schema (structured data) to product pages. This means your products appear in Google search results as plain blue links — while competitors using Shopify or custom sites show rich results with star ratings, prices in SAR, and stock availability.

These rich results significantly increase CTR. According to Google's own data, rich results can improve CTR by 20-40% for e-commerce pages.

Action: Add Product schema in JSON-LD format through Salla's custom code section in the theme settings, or use a Salla app that provides schema markup. The schema should include: product name, description, price with currency (SAR), price validity, availability status (in stock, out of stock, pre-order), brand, SKU or MPN, and any reviews with rating values.

Real result: For a Salla electronics store in Dammam, we added Product schema with pricing and availability information. Within 3 weeks, Google started showing their products with price tags and "In stock" labels in search results. Their organic CTR went from 2.1% to 4.8% — more than double. The schema implementation took under 2 hours.

Fix #5: Compensate with Off-Page SEO (Backlinks + Social)

Because Salla has inherent technical limitations in areas like URL structure, some schema types, and breadcrumb customization, you need to compensate with stronger off-page SEO signals. Google uses external signals to evaluate trust and authority, and Salla stores generally start with less inherent trust than custom-built or Shopify stores that have been around longer.

Action plan:

  • Build backlinks from Saudi business directories — Dalil, SaudiYP, local chamber of commerce sites, and industry-specific directories
  • Get your store URL listed on your Google Business Profile
  • Create social media content on Instagram, TikTok, and Snapchat that drives real traffic to your store (not just likes and views)
  • Consider guest posting on Saudi business blogs with links back to your store pages
  • Engage with customer reviews — both on your store and on external platforms — to build social proof signals

A Salla store with 20 quality backlinks from Saudi sources and an active social media presence will significantly outperform a Salla store with zero backlinks, even if their on-page SEO is identical. Technical SEO services can help identify and fix the specific limitations of your Salla setup.

The Salla SEO Prioritization Matrix

Time is limited, and you can't do everything at once. Here's the exact sequence we use:

  1. Fix product SEO titles (highest impact per hour — do this first for your 20 best-selling products)
  2. Write category descriptions (30 minutes per category, results within 4-8 weeks)
  3. Write custom meta descriptions for top 20 products (1 hour of work, 20-30% CTR lift)
  4. Set up Product schema (one-time technical task, 1-2 hours)
  5. Switch to a custom domain (if you haven't already — this is urgent)
  6. Build 5-10 quality backlinks from Saudi sources (ongoing, 2-3 hours per week)

Follow this sequence in order, and you will see measurable Google traffic growth within 60-90 days. We've seen it happen for 15+ Salla stores across different product categories — perfumes, electronics, fashion, beauty, home goods, and more.

The Frustration Is Real — But Completely Fixable

posts.title: Shopify vs Salla vs Zid: Which E-commerce Platform is Best for Your Saudi Business?
posts.excerpt: A detailed comparison of Shopify, Salla, and Zid — the three leading e-commerce platforms for Saudi businesses. We compare pricing, features, payment gateways, SEO, and scalability based on real experience.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
When building an online store in Saudi Arabia, you have three main options: Shopify (global leader), Salla (Saudi-built), and Zid (Saudi-grown with flexibility). Each platform has distinct advantages depending on your business size, technical needs, and growth plans. At BOSLA, we build on all three platforms. This comparison is based on our real experience working with Saudi merchants — not spec sheets. We know what actually works in the Saudi market because we have launched over 20 stores across all three platforms in the past year alone.

Payment Gateways

Shopify supports Mada, STC Pay, Apple Pay, and credit cards through Shopify Payments or third-party providers like Tap and Moyasar. Setup requires a bit of configuration for Saudi-specific gateways. You will need to install third-party apps which add $20-$50 per month in extra costs. The checkout process redirects customers to a payment page, which can cause a slight drop in conversion rates compared to native checkout.

Salla comes with built-in Mada, STC Pay, and credit card processing — no extra setup needed. This is Salla's strongest advantage for local merchants who want a plug-and-play payment experience. Customers complete checkout entirely within the store without any redirects, which significantly improves conversion rates. Salla also offers Tabby and Tamara integration out of the box.

Zid supports Mada, STC Pay, and credit cards through integrated gateways. Zid's payment setup is smoother than Shopify but slightly less turnkey than Salla. Zid offers good BNPL options with Tabby and Tamara built in. For most Saudi merchants, the native payment integration of Salla and Zid represents a significant advantage over Shopify's app-based approach.

Ease of Use

Salla is the easiest to use for Arabic-speaking business owners. The dashboard is fully in Arabic, and the platform is designed specifically for the Saudi market. You can launch a store in hours rather than days. Salla's customer support is in Arabic and responsive. For first-time store owners with no technical background, Salla is the clear winner in ease of use.

Shopify has a steeper learning curve, especially for Arabic speakers. The admin is English-first, though Arabic support exists. However, Shopify's app ecosystem is unmatched — thousands of apps for any feature you need. If you are comfortable working in English and want maximum flexibility, Shopify's learning curve is worth it.

Zid strikes a balance: Arabic-first dashboard with solid English support. It is more flexible than Salla but requires more setup time. Zid's support team is responsive and based in Riyadh, which is a plus for Saudi merchants who prefer local support.

SEO Capabilities

Shopify has the strongest SEO foundation — clean URL structure, fast CDN, built-in blogging, full control over meta tags, and excellent schema markup support. Shopify stores consistently rank well with proper optimization. If e-commerce SEO is your primary concern and you have the budget for professional optimization, Shopify gives you the most tools to work with.

Salla has good basic SEO features but limited control over advanced settings. URL structures are less flexible, and schema customization is restricted. For basic e-commerce SEO, it works well. For advanced strategies involving custom schema or complex URL structures, you will hit limitations that require creative workarounds.

Zid offers better SEO control than Salla but less than Shopify. Custom meta tags, URL structures, and schema injection are possible with some configuration work. For merchants who need more SEO control than Salla offers but prefer a Saudi-focused platform, Zid is the sweet spot.

Pricing Comparison

Shopify starts at $39 per month (Basic) with transaction fees of 2.9% + $0.30 unless you use Shopify Payments. App costs for Saudi-specific features can add $20-$100 per month. A fully equipped Shopify store with Saudi payment gateways and essential apps typically costs $80-$150 per month. Shopify also takes a cut of your revenue through transaction fees, which adds up significantly as you scale.

Salla starts at 149 SAR per month (Basic) with no transaction fees on most payment gateways. This makes it the most affordable option for Saudi startups. The 149 SAR plan includes everything you need to start selling — no paid apps required for local features. For a Saudi store doing 50,000 SAR in monthly sales, Salla's 149 SAR flat fee compares very favourably to Shopify's $79 Basic plan plus 2.9% transaction fees ($200+ per month total).

Zid starts at 249 SAR per month (Starter) and scales up based on features. No transaction fees on integrated gateways. Zid's pricing is higher than Salla but includes more built-in features and flexibility. For growing businesses that need more than Salla's basic plan but want to stay in the Saudi ecosystem, Zid offers good value.

Which Platform Should You Choose?

Choose Salla if: You are a Saudi startup or small business that wants the fastest path to launch. Salla's Arabic-first experience and built-in local features make it the most beginner-friendly option. Salla store setup service Choose Shopify if: You plan to scale internationally, need advanced apps and integrations, or want the best SEO foundation. Choose Zid if: You need more flexibility than Salla offers but want a Saudi-focused platform with local support.

posts.title: WordPress vs Custom Website Development: Which is Right for Your Business?
posts.excerpt: Compare WordPress websites vs custom-built websites for Saudi businesses. Learn which approach works best for your budget, timeline, and feature requirements.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
One of the most common questions we hear is: should I use WordPress or build a custom website? The answer depends on your budget, timeline, feature needs, and long-term goals. Both approaches have clear advantages and trade-offs. At BOSLA, we build both WordPress sites and custom web applications. We recommend based on what actually serves your business best — not what is technically flashier. Here is our honest comparison based on real projects we have delivered for Saudi businesses across Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, and other cities.

Time to Launch

WordPress: A standard WordPress site can be launched in 1-3 weeks. With thousands of themes and plugins available, we can rapidly build a professional site without writing everything from scratch. For businesses that need to launch quickly — perhaps for an upcoming marketing campaign or seasonal promotion — WordPress is almost always the faster option. We recently launched a 5-page corporate site for a logistics company in Dammam in just 5 business days using WordPress with a customised theme.

Custom Build: A custom-built website typically takes 4-12 weeks depending on complexity. Every feature is built from the ground up, which takes more development time. However, you get exactly what you want with no compromises. For businesses with unique requirements that cannot be met by existing plugins or themes, the extra time is well worth it.

Cost Comparison

WordPress: A professional WordPress site starts from 1,000 SAR for a simple corporate site with 5 pages. WooCommerce stores for e-commerce range from 2,000-4,000 SAR depending on the number of products and payment gateway integrations. website maintenance packages

Custom Build: Custom websites start from 5,000 SAR and can go up to 20,000+ SAR for complex applications with custom features, integrations, and databases. There are no recurring plugin license fees, but development costs are significantly higher upfront. For most SMEs, the cost difference makes WordPress the more practical choice.

Flexibility and Customization

WordPress: With 60,000+ plugins and thousands of themes, WordPress can handle almost any standard website requirement — contact forms, blogs, e-commerce, booking systems, membership sites, and more. For 90% of business websites, WordPress offers all the flexibility you need. However, if you need a feature that does not exist as a plugin, you may face compatibility issues or performance compromises.

Custom Build: Unlimited flexibility. You can build any feature, any design, any integration exactly as you envision it. Custom builds are ideal for businesses with unique workflows, complex data models, or specific performance requirements that WordPress cannot meet efficiently. Businesses in sectors like healthcare, logistics, or finance often benefit from custom solutions.

SEO and Performance

WordPress: With proper optimization, WordPress sites perform excellently on SEO. Popular SEO plugins like Yoast and Rank Math provide comprehensive control over meta tags, sitemaps, and schema markup. Performance depends heavily on hosting quality, theme choice, and plugin management. A well-optimized WordPress site can score 90+ on Google PageSpeed. We always pair WordPress builds with technical SEO optimization to ensure strong foundation.

Custom Build: Custom sites can be optimized for maximum performance since there is no code bloat from plugins. Developers have full control over every line of code, which means faster load times and cleaner SEO implementation. However, achieving this requires an experienced development team.

Maintenance and Support

WordPress: Requires regular updates for the core platform, themes, and plugins. Budget 200-500 SAR per month for managed maintenance that includes security updates, backups, and performance monitoring. Without regular updates, WordPress sites become vulnerable to security threats within 6-12 months. We recommend our maintenance and support services for ongoing peace of mind.

Custom Build: Requires less frequent updates but when changes are needed, they require developer involvement. There is no automatic update system like WordPress, so maintenance costs depend on the complexity of changes needed. Custom builds are generally more secure out of the box since they are not a common target for automated attacks.

Which Should You Choose?

Choose WordPress if: You want a cost-effective site launched quickly. You need a blog or content management system that your team can manage without developer assistance. Your requirements are standard and well-supported by existing plugins and themes. For most Saudi SMEs, this is the smartest choice.

Choose Custom if: You have unique business workflows that no existing plugin can handle. You need maximum performance with zero code bloat. You are building a complex web application rather than a content site. You have a larger budget (5,000 SAR+) and a timeline of 4-12 weeks. For most Saudi SMEs, WordPress offers the best balance of cost, speed, and flexibility. Custom builds make sense for businesses with unique workflows, complex data models, or specific performance requirements that off-the-shelf solutions cannot meet.

Need help deciding? We offer free consultations to understand your actual needs and recommend the right approach for your specific project.

posts.title: How a Riyadh Fashion Boutique Increased Sales 3x with a Salla Store
posts.excerpt: A family-run fashion boutique in Riyadh transformed their business by moving from Instagram sales to a professional Salla e-commerce store with SEO and social media advertising.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
The Client

Noora Fashion Boutique is a family-run fashion retailer based in Riyadh, specializing in modest women's fashion and abayas. They had been operating for three years primarily through Instagram DMs and WhatsApp orders. Despite having 15,000+ followers and strong engagement, they were struggling to convert their social media following into steady, scalable revenue. The founder, Nora Al-Saud, was spending over 30 hours per week just on manual order management — responding to customer inquiries, sending bank account details, tracking payments, and coordinating delivery through WhatsApp.

The Challenge

The boutique was losing sales every day because their sales process was entirely manual. Customers would browse products on Instagram, message the store to inquire about availability and pricing, wait for a response that could take hours during busy periods, and then arrange payment manually through bank transfer. This multi-step process resulted in a high abandonment rate. Many customers lost interest waiting for replies. Others found the manual payment process too complicated and bought from competitors with proper online stores. The boutique had no way to recover abandoned carts, no automated inventory tracking, and no professional product catalog. As the business grew, managing orders through DMs became completely unsustainable.

The Solution

We built a complete Salla e-commerce store with integrated Mada and STC Pay for seamless Saudi payments. We migrated their full product catalog of 200+ items with professional Arabic descriptions, optimized images, and proper categorization. We implemented automated order confirmation and tracking via SMS and WhatsApp, which eliminated the need for manual follow-up. We also set up Snapchat ad campaigns targeting Riyadh-based fashion shoppers aged 18-35, and integrated inventory management to prevent overselling.

The Results

  • 300% increase in monthly sales within 3 months of launch
  • Zero abandoned carts due to streamlined, one-click checkout
  • 40% reduction in customer service workload via automated order tracking
  • First page Google ranking for key Arabic search terms within 8 weeks
  • Average order value increased 25% through product recommendations and bundles

What the Client Says

"BOSLA transformed our business. We went from manually managing orders on Instagram to a fully automated store. Our customers love the seamless checkout experience, and I have been able to focus on sourcing new products instead of answering DMs all day." — Nora Al-Saud, Founder

If you are running your business through Instagram DMs and WhatsApp, you could be leaving significant revenue on the table. A professional online store with proper payment gateways and automated operations can transform your business just like it did for Noora Fashion Boutique.

The Implementation Process

We followed a structured 4-week implementation plan. Week 1 focused on platform selection and store design — we chose Salla specifically for its native Saudi payment integration and Arabic-first dashboard. Week 2 involved product migration with professional photography guidelines and SEO-optimized descriptions. Week 3 covered payment gateway setup, shipping configuration, and automated notification systems. Week 4 was dedicated to testing, staff training, and launching the advertising campaign.

Key Decisions That Made the Difference

Three decisions were critical. First, choosing Salla over Shopify: Nora had zero technical experience, and Salla's Arabic dashboard meant she could manage the store independently from day one. Second, investing in professional product photography — the boutique's abayas needed high-quality images to compete with established retailers. Third, integrating automated WhatsApp notifications for order confirmations and shipping updates eliminated the most time-consuming part of their manual process.

Lessons for Other Saudi Businesses

Start with the payment experience — Saudi customers expect Mada and STC Pay, and seamless checkout is the highest-impact change. Automate customer communication before adding new sales channels. Invest in product presentation — on a professional store, photos and descriptions replace the in-person sales conversation. Plan for growth from day one by choosing a platform that scales with you.

E-commerce SEO and social media ads work together to drive sustainable, scalable growth.

Why This Project Matters for Saudi Businesses

The Noora Fashion Boutique case is not unique. We see this pattern repeatedly across Saudi Arabia: businesses that start on Instagram or WhatsApp reach a ceiling where manual processes prevent further growth. The transition to a professional e-commerce platform is not just about having a website — it is about fundamentally changing how you operate. Automated order processing, professional payment handling, and systematic marketing open growth channels that are simply not available through social media alone. For Saudi businesses, the key is choosing a platform that handles local requirements natively — Mada payments, Arabic interface, local shipping integration — rather than forcing a global platform to work in the local context.

What We Would Do Differently Next Time

With hindsight, we would have prioritized social media advertising integration earlier in the process. The Snapchat ad campaign launched in week 4 could have begun in week 2 with a pre-launch teaser strategy, building anticipation and an email list before the store went live. We would also have set up a customer loyalty program from the start — the boutique's repeat customer rate was high, and a formal loyalty program with points and rewards would have increased average customer lifetime value significantly. These improvements would have accelerated the already impressive 300% sales increase even further.

posts.title: A Jeddah Medical Clinic Tripled Patient Inquiries with Local SEO
posts.excerpt: A multi-specialty clinic in Jeddah needed more local patients. After our SEO overhaul, they became the top-ranked clinic in their area on Google Maps and search.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
The Client

Al-Salam Medical Complex is a multi-specialty healthcare provider in Jeddah offering dermatology, dental, and general medicine services. They had been operating for over 10 years with a steady stream of walk-in patients but wanted to grow their patient base through online bookings and local search visibility. Despite having excellent doctors and modern facilities, they were invisible to the growing number of patients who search for healthcare services on Google.

The Challenge

WordPress website development that was over 5 years old. It was painfully slow — loading in 8+ seconds on mobile devices where most of their potential patients browse. The site was not mobile-friendly, had poor content, and was barely visible on Google. They were ranking 12th or worse for critical searches like "dermatologist in Jeddah" and "dentist south Jeddah." Their Google Business Profile was unclaimed with only 2 old reviews, no photos, and incorrect business hours. Patients actively searching for medical services in their area simply could not find them online, while competitors with better online presence were capturing those patients.

The Solution

We redesigned their WordPress site with a mobile-first approach prioritizing speed and user experience, implemented a comprehensive local SEO strategy with dedicated landing pages for each medical specialty and service area, optimized and fully claimed their Google Business Profile with accurate categories, high-quality photos of the facility, and regular posts, built consistent local citations across 20+ Saudi healthcare and business directories, and launched targeted Google Ads campaigns for high-intent medical keywords like "أفضل دكتور جلدية في جدة" and "تركيب تقويم أسنان جنوب جدة."

The Results

  • 450% increase in organic traffic within 4 months of launch
  • Top 3 Google Maps ranking for 12 medical keywords in their area
  • 3x increase in phone call inquiries month-over-month
  • Google Ads achieving 8%+ conversion rate on appointment bookings
  • 12 new patient reviews on Google within the first 2 months

What the Client Says

"The difference is night and day. We used to rely entirely on walk-in patients and word of mouth. Now most of our new patients find us through Google. Our phone has not stopped ringing since BOSLA optimized our online presence. The investment paid for itself within the first month." — Dr. Abdulaziz Al-Harbi, Director

If your clinic or medical practice is not showing up on Google when patients search for your services, you are losing them to competitors who have invested in local SEO. It is the most cost-effective way to attract more patients in your area.

The Implementation Process

The project unfolded over 8 weeks across four phases. Phase 1 (weeks 1-2): We audited the existing site, identified critical issues including slow page speed and missing meta tags, and conducted local keyword research for medical services in Jeddah. Phase 2 (weeks 3-4): We rebuilt the WordPress site mobile-first, optimized for Core Web Vitals with under 2 second loading time. Phase 3 (weeks 5-6): We implemented the local SEO strategy with 15 service-specific landing pages and citations across Saudi medical directories. Phase 4 (weeks 7-8): We launched Google Ads campaigns and began monitoring organic performance.

The Google Business Profile Transformation

The clinic's Google Business Profile was the single highest-impact fix. Before: unclaimed profile with 2 old reviews, no photos, and incorrect hours. After: complete profile with 20+ high-quality photos, accurate categories for all specialities, weekly posts sharing health tips, and a systematic review process that added 12 new 5-star reviews in two months. The profile went from invisible to top 3 in local pack results for 12 medical keywords.

Measurable Outcomes

Beyond headline numbers: online appointment bookings increased from 5 to over 80 per month, phone inquiries tripled, bounce rate dropped from 78% to 34%, and average session duration increased from 45 seconds to 3 minutes 20 seconds. Google Ads achieved a cost-per-click of 3.50 SAR and 8.2% conversion rate.

Why Local SEO Works So Well for Saudi Healthcare

Healthcare is inherently local. Patients rarely travel across cities for routine medical care — they search for clinics and doctors near their home or workplace. This makes local SEO exceptionally effective for Saudi medical practices. The key insight from this project is that most clinics in Saudi Arabia still have unoptimized or unclaimed Google Business Profiles. Simply claiming and fully optimizing the profile creates an immediate competitive advantage. When combined with a fast, mobile-friendly website and targeted local content, the results are dramatic. For the 10+ clinics we have worked with across Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, the average increase in patient inquiries after implementing a full local SEO strategy is 200-400% within 4-6 months.

Scaling the Model to Other Specialities

The approach we used for Al-Salam Medical Complex is replicable across any healthcare speciality — dental clinics, dermatology centers, physiotherapy practices, and specialized medical centers all benefit from the same strategy. The specific keywords change (orthodontist vs dermatologist vs physiotherapist) but the framework remains the same: technical SEO fixes, mobile-first redesign, complete GBP optimization, local citation building, and targeted Google Ads for high-intent medical searches. Each additional speciality or location adds incremental patients with minimal additional effort.

posts.title: From Home Kitchen to Dammam Most Popular Online Gourmet Store
posts.excerpt: A home-based gourmet food business scaled to a full e-commerce operation using Shopify, with delivery across Dammam and Khobar.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
The Client

Gourmet House started as a home kitchen in Dammam, selling premium gourmet sauces, spice blends, and artisanal food products. The founder began by taking orders through WhatsApp from friends and family, and the business grew purely through word of mouth and Instagram posts. Within a year, demand had grown beyond what a home kitchen and manual order system could handle.

The Challenge

As demand grew rapidly, managing orders manually through WhatsApp became chaotic and unsustainable. The founder was spending 4+ hours daily just responding to messages, tracking orders in a notebook, and manually calculating delivery fees based on location. There was no proper product catalog showing the full product range, no way to showcase new products effectively, no automated payment processing, and no system for managing delivery zones across Dammam and Khobar. Customers frequently complained about slow response times and delivery confusion. The business had clearly outgrown its home kitchen model but lacked the digital infrastructure to scale effectively without adding more manual work.

The Solution

We built a Shopify e-commerce store with a premium design that reflected their gourmet brand positioning, designed a complete brand identity including logo, packaging design, and cohesive color system, set up automated delivery zones for Dammam and Khobar with shipping calculations based on distance, integrated Mada and STC Pay for seamless checkout, and created a content marketing strategy featuring recipe blog posts and professional food photography that showcased their products in use.

The Results

  • 200+ monthly orders within the first 2 months of launch
  • Average order value increased 45% through strategic product bundling and upsells
  • Instagram following grew organically from 2,000 to 12,000 in 3 months through consistent content
  • Featured in 3 Saudi food blogs and local media outlets
  • Customer satisfaction improved dramatically with automated order confirmations and tracking

What the Client Says

"Going from a notebook and WhatsApp to a professional online store felt like a dream. Our customers love the new brand identity and the easy ordering process. We have been able to focus on making great food instead of managing orders." — Founder, Gourmet House

If you are running a food business through WhatsApp and struggling to keep up with demand, a professional e-commerce store with automated ordering and delivery management can help you scale without the chaos. Online store development combined with strong branding and a content strategy creates a powerful foundation for growth.

The Implementation Process

This project required a 5-week timeline. Week 1: brand identity development including logo, color palette, typography, and packaging design guidelines. Week 2: Shopify store development with a custom theme reflecting the gourmet brand. Week 3: product catalog setup with 80+ products, food photography guidelines, and SEO-optimized descriptions. Week 4: Mada and STC Pay integration, automated delivery zones for Dammam and Khobar, and WhatsApp notification system. Week 5: content creation including recipe blog posts and the launch marketing plan.

The Brand Identity Impact

Building a cohesive brand identity was transformative. Previously operating without a logo, the business now had professional packaging that customers photographed and shared on social media — turning every order into free marketing. The branded packaging and consistent Instagram aesthetic helped the account grow from 2,000 to 12,000 followers organically. Customers mentioned that professional branding made them confident ordering from a home-based business, addressing the trust barrier small food businesses face.

Operational Transformation

Order management automation was the most impactful change. Before: 4+ hours daily on manual tasks. After: fully automated order processing with instant WhatsApp confirmations, auto-calculated delivery fees, and real-time inventory tracking. Daily administrative time dropped from 4+ hours to under 30 minutes, allowing the founder to focus on recipe development, quality control, and business growth.

Why Branding Matters for Saudi Food Businesses

The Gourmet House case demonstrates a crucial lesson for Saudi food businesses: branding is not a luxury, it is a growth driver. When we started, the business had no logo, no cohesive visual identity, and inconsistent social media presence. After the brand transformation, customers began sharing product photos on social media organically, creating a word-of-mouth marketing engine that no amount of paid advertising could replicate. For Saudi food businesses operating from home kitchens or small commercial spaces, professional branding signals quality and reliability — two factors that overcome the natural hesitation customers feel when ordering from an unknown producer. posts.title: How to Start an Online Store in Saudi Arabia: A Step-by-Step Guide for 2026
posts.excerpt: You want to sell online but have no idea where to start. Platform, payments, shipping, legal — here is exactly what to do in order, with real costs for each step.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
Ahmad had been selling perfumes through his Instagram account for two years. He had 8,000 followers, consistent engagement, and a growing customer base. But every day was the same struggle — customers would comment asking about prices and availability, and he would spend hours responding to DMs, sending bank account numbers, and manually tracking orders in a notebook. He knew he needed a proper online store, but every time he searched "how to start an online store in Saudi Arabia," he found conflicting advice. Three months later, he was still on Instagram, still losing sales to competitors with proper stores. If this sounds familiar, you are not alone. This guide walks you through exactly what to do in the right order.

E-commerce platform setup

Your platform choice is the most important decision. It determines your monthly costs, which payment gateways you can use, how your store looks on mobile, and how easy it is to manage daily operations. In Saudi Arabia, you have three strong options. Salla is the most popular choice for Saudi startups. It costs 149 SAR per month, comes with Mada and STC Pay built in, and has a fully Arabic dashboard. You can launch a basic store in 2-3 days. Shopify costs $39 per month (about 150 SAR) plus transaction fees and requires third-party apps for Saudi payment gateways. It is best if you plan to sell internationally or need advanced customization. Zid costs 249 SAR per month and offers a middle ground — Arabic interface with more flexibility than Salla. For most new Saudi merchants, we recommend starting with Salla as the fastest and most affordable path to launch.

Step 2: Register Your Business

To accept payments and build customer trust, you need proper business registration. At minimum, you need a Commercial Registration (CR) from the Ministry of Commerce. You also need to register with ZATCA for VAT if your annual revenue exceeds 375,000 SAR. For specific product categories like food, cosmetics, or health items, additional permits from the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) may be required. Many new store owners skip this step and later face issues with payment gateway approval and customer trust.

Step 3: Set Up Payment Gateways

Saudi customers expect to pay with Mada, STC Pay, Apple Pay, and increasingly with Buy Now Pay Later options like Tabby and Tamara. If your store only offers credit card payments, you will lose a significant portion of potential customers. Each payment gateway requires a separate application and approval process. Mada integration through providers like Tap, Moyasar, or HyperPay typically takes 1-2 weeks for approval. STC Pay has a similar timeline. Tabby and Tamara applications may take longer depending on your business documentation.

Step 4: Set Up Shipping and Logistics

In Saudi Arabia, Cash on Delivery still accounts for 30-50% of e-commerce orders. You need a shipping partner who can handle COD collections reliably. Major options include SMSA for comprehensive Saudi coverage, Aramex for both domestic and international shipping, and Naqel for reliable nationwide delivery. For local delivery within a single city, services like Mrsool and Luggzy work well for restaurants and perishable goods. Factor shipping costs into your pricing strategy — many Saudi stores offer free shipping above a certain order value to encourage larger purchases.

Step 5: Add Products Optimized for Search

This is where most new store owners make their biggest mistake. They upload products with generic descriptions copied from suppliers and wonder why nobody visits their store. Each product needs a unique title that includes relevant search keywords, a detailed description that answers customer questions, high-quality images from multiple angles, proper categorization within your store structure, and SEO metadata including meta title and description for Google. E-commerce SEO is critical for getting found by customers searching on Google. Stores that invest in SEO from day one see significantly better results than those that try to add it later.

Starting an online store in Saudi Arabia is an exciting journey with enormous potential. The Saudi e-commerce market is projected to grow to nearly $50 billion by 2030. The businesses that succeed are the ones that take action — they pick a platform, set up properly, and start selling. They do not wait for perfection. If you need help with any part of this process, we offer free consultations to guide you through platform selection, store setup, SEO, and marketing strategy. Online store setup does not need to be complicated when you have the right partner.

Common Mistakes New Store Owners Make

The most common mistake is launching before the store is ready — missing payment gateways, incomplete product descriptions, and no shipping setup. The second is choosing a platform based on price alone without considering long-term needs. Salla at 149 SAR/month is great for starting, but for 10,000+ products or international sales, Shopify may be worth the higher complexity. The third mistake is neglecting SEO before launch — optimizing product titles, descriptions, and meta tags during setup is far easier than fixing them later.

posts.title: The Complete Guide to SEO for Saudi Businesses: What Actually Works in 2026
posts.excerpt: Every agency promises page 1 rankings. But SEO is confusing and results take months. Here is exactly what matters for a Saudi business — and what is a waste of money.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
A furniture store owner in Riyadh paid 15,000 SAR to an SEO agency. Six months later, his site was still on page 8 of Google. The agency had built hundreds of low-quality backlinks from spam websites, stuffed keywords into invisible text, and created 50 blog posts of obvious AI-generated content. Google penalized his site instead of ranking it. Stories like this are unfortunately common in Saudi Arabia. Many agencies sell SEO packages that do more harm than good. This guide cuts through the noise and tells you exactly what matters for your Saudi business.

Pillar 1: Technical SEO

Technical SEO is the foundation. If Google cannot crawl and index your site properly, nothing else matters. The essentials: your site must load in under 2.5 seconds on mobile (this is Google's Core Web Vitals standard), every page must have unique meta titles and descriptions, your site must have an XML sitemap submitted to Google Search Console, every page needs a self-referencing canonical tag to avoid duplicate content issues, and your robots.txt file must not accidentally block important pages. Technical SEO services cover all of these technical fundamentals. We often find that fixing technical issues alone can improve rankings significantly within weeks.

Pillar 2: Local SEO

For most Saudi businesses, local SEO delivers the fastest return on investment. When someone in Riyadh searches for "شركة تصميم مواقع في الرياض," Google shows local results first — the map pack with three businesses, followed by local organic results. To rank here, you need a fully optimized Google Business Profile with accurate categories, correct business hours, high-quality photos, regular posts, and genuine customer reviews. You also need consistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) information across all online directories. Local SEO optimization also involves building citations on Saudi-specific directories like دليل الأعمال and دليل السعودية. A well-optimized local presence can triple your inbound inquiries, as we have seen with clinics, restaurants, and service businesses across the Kingdom.

Pillar 3: Content SEO

Content is how Google understands what your website is about. Every page on your site should target one specific topic and cover it thoroughly. Write for humans first — answer their questions, address their concerns, provide actionable information. Then make sure your content naturally includes the words and phrases real customers use when searching. A well-written service page that answers common customer questions will outperform a keyword-stuffed page every single time. Content SEO is about creating genuinely useful content that positions you as an authority in your field. Google's algorithms have become sophisticated enough to distinguish between content written for humans and content written purely for rankings.

Pillar 4: Link Building

Backlinks from reputable Saudi websites tell Google that your site is trustworthy and authoritative. Focus on earning links from Saudi business directories, local news websites covering your industry, industry associations and chambers of commerce, guest posts on relevant Saudi blogs and publications, and partnerships with complementary businesses. A single link from a reputable Saudi source like a well-known industry publication is worth more than 100 links from low-quality international directories. Link building services should focus on quality over quantity — a principle many agencies ignore.

What Is a Waste of Money

Avoid any agency that promises page 1 results in 30 days — real SEO takes 3-6 months to show meaningful impact. Avoid bulk backlink packages selling 500 links for 500 SAR — these are almost always spam and can get your site penalized by Google. Avoid keyword stuffing and hidden text techniques that were outdated in 2010. Avoid content that is obviously AI-generated without human editing and fact-checking.

How to Start

The smartest first step is an SEO audit to understand your current position and identify the biggest opportunities. A professional audit will tell you exactly what technical issues need fixing, what keywords you could realistically rank for, and what your competitors are doing well. From there, you can build a phased plan that prioritizes fixes by impact. SEO is a long-term investment that compounds over time. The earlier you start doing it properly, the harder it becomes for competitors to catch up.

Common SEO Mistakes Saudi Businesses Make

We have seen the same SEO mistakes repeated across dozens of Saudi businesses. The most damaging: hiring agencies that promise fast results through questionable tactics like buying low-quality backlinks, keyword stuffing, or creating AI-generated content at scale. These tactics may show short-term improvements but almost always result in Google penalties that take months to recover from. Other common mistakes include neglecting mobile optimization (over 80% of Saudi searches are on mobile), ignoring local SEO (most Saudi businesses serve local customers but optimize for national keywords), and failing to update content regularly (Google prefers fresh, regularly updated content). The safest approach is steady, white-hat SEO focused on creating genuinely useful content, earning legitimate backlinks from Saudi sources, and providing an excellent user experience on mobile devices.

posts.title: 5 Signs Your Website Is Driving Customers Away (And How to Fix Each One)
posts.excerpt: Your website might be the reason you are losing customers — and you do not even know it. Here are the 5 most common mistakes we fix for Saudi businesses.
posts.author: BOSLA Team
posts.content:
A dental clinic in Riyadh was spending 8,000 SAR per month on Google Ads. They were getting clicks, but almost zero conversions. New patients would click the ad, land on the clinic's website, and leave within 5 seconds. The problem was not the ads — the website took 8 seconds to load on mobile, had no contact information above the fold, and the booking form required 12 fields. The clinic was paying good money to bring visitors to a site that actively pushed them away. Your website might be doing the same thing. Here are the 5 most common mistakes we fix for Saudi businesses, and exactly how to fix each one.

Sign #1: Your Site Loads Too Slowly

If your site takes more than 3 seconds to load on mobile, over 50% of visitors will leave before seeing anything. In Saudi Arabia, where mobile internet usage is among the highest in the world, speed is critical. We have seen clinics, restaurants, and e-commerce stores losing 60-80% of potential customers because of slow loading times. The fix: compress all images to WebP format, enable browser caching, use a CDN with Saudi servers, minimize CSS and JavaScript, and upgrade to faster hosting. A simple speed optimization can cut loading time from 8 seconds to under 2 seconds. Technical SEO services include comprehensive speed optimization as a core component.

Sign #2: Contact Information Is Hidden

Saudi customers prefer WhatsApp over email or contact forms. If your WhatsApp number is buried in the footer, customers will leave and find a competitor who makes it easy to reach them. The fix: place your WhatsApp button prominently in the header and on every page. Display your phone number in the top bar. Show your physical address with a Google Maps embed. Make it possible for a customer to contact you within 2 seconds of landing on your site. We always include prominent WhatsApp integration in every custom website we build.

Sign #3: Your Site Does Not Work Well on Mobile

Over 80% of Saudi internet users browse on mobile phones. If your site looks good on a laptop but is hard to use on a phone — tiny buttons, text requiring zoom, images not resizing — you are alienating most of your potential customers. The fix: test your site on real mobile devices, ensure buttons are at least 48x48 pixels for touch targets, use responsive design, and run Google's Mobile-Friendly Test. Website redesign services often focus heavily on mobile optimization as a primary goal.

Sign #4: Content Does Not Answer Customer Questions

When customers visit your site, they have specific questions: How much does this cost? How long does it take? Do you serve my area? If your site does not answer these questions clearly and immediately, the customer leaves to find a competitor who does. The fix: add an FAQ section to every service page, include pricing info or ranges, mention service areas explicitly, and write content that anticipates and answers questions before they are asked. Well-structured content that answers real customer questions is the foundation of effective SEO.

Sign #5: No Clear Call to Action

A visitor reads your content but does not know what to do next. Should they call? WhatsApp? Fill a form? Book a consultation? If the next step is unclear, they will leave and find a competitor who makes it obvious. Every page on your site should have one primary action you want visitors to take, and that action should be visible without scrolling. For service businesses, the primary CTA should be WhatsApp or phone call — Saudi customers prefer direct communication. For e-commerce, it should be Add to Cart or Buy Now. For content pages, it could be a free consultation booking or downloading a resource. Test different CTA placements and wording to find what converts best for your specific audience.
